summary: The moon at a phase of its cycle (0 new, 0.25 first quarter, 0.5 full, 0.75 last quarter), drawn from circles, a half-disc and an elliptical terminator in a square canvas.

phase.doc: 0..1 through the lunation: 0 new, 0.125 waxing crescent, 0.25 first quarter, 0.5 full, 0.75 last quarter. A number, a "@variable" or an expression (computed from the clock in the document); it wraps, so a lunation count works too

size.doc: Width and height in dp; the drawing is on a 100-unit box scaled to it

rim.doc: A 1 dp ring around the disc, so a new moon is still a visible circle

label.doc: Accessibility label; say the phase name when the document computes it

pitfalls: Don't draw a moon as a text glyph (🌒 ◐ ☾): it depends on the device's fonts, can't take theme colours or a size, and shows eight phases at best. Call MoonPhase with the phase computed in the document
Waxing is lit on the right (phase < 0.5) and waning on the left, as seen from the northern hemisphere; for the southern hemisphere mirror it (a scale of -1 around the centre) or pass 1 - phase
phase is the fraction of the lunation, not the fraction lit: the lit fraction is (1 - cos(2π · phase)) / 2, so a quarter moon (0.25) is half lit, and 0.125 is about 15% lit

The terminator is an ellipse of half-width r · |cos(2π · phase)|, in the shade colour for a crescent (cos > 0) and in the lit colour for a gibbous moon (cos < 0). Each is drawn with a width of max(0, ±cos), so the other one has zero width: no paint alpha to switch and reset
At exactly new moon the lit half isn't drawn (its sweep is 180 · step(0.9999, cos)): the shaded ellipse covers it, but the half-disc's antialiased edge would still leave a lit hairline on the limb
The edge ring is a disc 1 dp larger drawn first, not a stroke drawn last: a stroke over the disc dulls the lit limb

Mono ignores lit, shade and rim: the lit part is onSurface and the rest background inside a 1.5 dp outline ring, so the phase reads as shape. On black (mono) that is a white full moon; in mono inverted (e-ink) the lit part is the ink, so a full moon is a black disc, the reverse of a printed almanac's ● new / ○ full: label the phases there
